title: Shot, Reverse Shot
objective: After this level you can explain how shot, reverse shot and eyeline matches build a conversation out of separate shots.
summary: Shot/reverse shot alternates between characters in a conversation, joined by eyeline matches: a look off-screen, then what is seen. Because it is assembled, the editor shapes the performances.

cards.headline: In many film conversations, you see one face at a time.
cards.body: One face talks. Cut. The other face listens. Cut back. You feel as if you're sitting at the table with them, but you're watching separate shots taking turns. How does a string of single faces add up to two people talking to each other?

cards.headline: Taking turns: shot, reverse shot
cards.body: The pattern is called shot/reverse shot: two or more shots edited together that alternate between characters, typically in a conversation. Each character is often shown in a close-up of their own, and the cuts usually follow the flow of the dialogue. It's like watching a tennis rally from the stands: your attention passes back and forth with the ball.

cards.headline: Where they look tells you where they are
cards.body: What glues the separate close-ups together is the eyeline match. One shot shows a person looking off-screen in one direction; the next shows what they see. Direction matters: if she looks left, the next shot implies she's off-screen to the right, looking at him. Get the eyelines right and two faces, shown separately, seem to meet across the table.

cards.headline: The editor shapes the acting, too
cards.body: Because the conversation is assembled, the editor gets a say in it. Staying on the speaker gives a line one tone; cutting to the listener's reaction gives the same line another. Editors trim the ends of shots so an actor seems to jump in on someone's line, or draw out a pause. Viewers credit the actors with much of what the editor built.

cards.headline: Conversations: assembled
learned: Shot/reverse shot: alternating characters in a conversation
Eyeline match: a look off-screen, then what is seen
Looks left in one shot, sits off-screen right in the next
Cutting to reactions and trimming pauses shapes the acting

options.label: Shots that alternate between characters in a conversation
One long shot that swings from speaker to speaker
options.rationale: Shot/reverse shot is built from separate shots joined by cuts.

options.label: A shot played backward for effect
options.rationale: "Reverse" means the other side of the conversation, not backward.

options.label: A film's opening shot repeated at its end
options.rationale: It's about alternating characters, not repeating shots.

questions.explanation: Shot/reverse shot alternates shots of the characters, typically in a conversation, often in close-ups.

questions.explanation: Shot/reverse shot alternates between characters, an eyeline match shows a look and then what the person sees, and editors trim the ends of shots to shape the acting.

questions.prompt: Level 33 kept characters on steady sides of the frame. In shot/reverse shot, if she looks left, she is implied to be _____.

options.label: off-screen to the left
options.rationale: She looks left toward him, so she sits to his right.

options.label: directly behind the camera
options.rationale: The eyeline puts her to one side, not behind.

options.label: in the same shot as him
options.rationale: In shot/reverse shot, each is shown separately.

questions.explanation: If the person looks left, the next shot implies the looker is off-screen right, matching the 180-degree rule.
